topics.title: React Router Basics
topics.summary: React Router maps URLs to components so a single-page app can have multiple "pages" without reloads.
topics.description:
A single-page app (SPA) has one HTML file. **Client-side routing** changes what is rendered when the URL changes, using the History API, without a full page reload. **React Router** is the standard library. Version 6 introduced the current API; **version 7** merges it with Remix (import from `react-router`, with an optional framework mode) and keeps the same core ideas.

### Core pieces

| Piece | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `BrowserRouter` | enables routing with clean URLs |
| `Routes` / `Route` | match the URL to an `element` |
| `Link` | navigation without page reload (renders `<a>`) |
| `NavLink` | Link that knows if it is active (`isActive`) |
| `Navigate` | redirect declaratively |
| `path="*"` | catch-all, used for 404 pages |

### Setup

```jsx
import { BrowserRouter, Routes, Route, Link } from "react-router-dom";

<BrowserRouter>
  <nav><Link to="/">Home</Link> <Link to="/about">About</Link></nav>
  <Routes>
    <Route path="/" element={<Home />} />
    <Route path="/about" element={<About />} />
    <Route path="*" element={<NotFound />} />
  </Routes>
</BrowserRouter>
```

### Notes

- Use `Link`, never a plain `<a href>`, for internal navigation (a plain anchor reloads the page).
- Routes match by **best specificity**, not order.
- Relative links resolve against the route they are rendered in.
- For static hosts, configure a **fallback to index.html** so refreshing `/about` does not return 404.
- `HashRouter` is an alternative for hosts without rewrite rules.
keyPoints: Client-side routing changes the view without reloading
Routes/Route map paths to elements; path="*" is 404
Use Link / NavLink instead of <a> for internal links
BrowserRouter needs server fallback to index.html
v7 imports from react-router; same core API
pitfalls: Using <a href> for internal pages, causing full reloads.
Deploying without SPA fallback, so refreshing a deep link gives 404.

topics.title: Nested Routes and Layouts
topics.summary: Nest routes so shared layout (header, sidebar) stays while only the inner part changes, using Outlet.
topics.description:
Real apps share layouts: a navbar and footer on every page, a sidebar on dashboard pages. Nested routes express this directly in the route tree.

```jsx
<Routes>
  <Route element={<MainLayout />}>
    <Route index element={<Home />} />
    <Route path="products" element={<Products />} />
    <Route path="dashboard" element={<DashboardLayout />}>
      <Route index element={<Overview />} />
      <Route path="settings" element={<Settings />} />
    </Route>
  </Route>
  <Route path="*" element={<NotFound />} />
</Routes>
```

### Outlet

A parent route renders `<Outlet />` where its matched child should appear:

```jsx
function MainLayout() {
  return (
    <>
      <Header />
      <main><Outlet /></main>
      <Footer />
    </>
  );
}
```

### Concepts

- **Layout routes**: a route with no `path` (only `element`) used purely for layout and shared logic.
- **Index routes**: `index` renders at the parent's exact URL.
- **Relative paths**: child `path="settings"` becomes `/dashboard/settings`.
- **Outlet context**: `<Outlet context={...} />` passes data to children via `useOutletContext()`.
- **Pathless routes** group routes for guards without changing the URL.

### Benefits

State inside the layout is preserved while navigating between its children, and you avoid duplicating headers in every page component.

Index route renders at the parent path

Child paths are relative to the parent

pitfalls: Forgetting <Outlet />, so child routes never appear.
Using absolute paths on children accidentally (leading slash resets the nesting).

topics.title: Params, Search Params and Navigation
topics.summary: Read URL parameters with useParams, query strings with useSearchParams, and navigate in code with useNavigate.
topics.description:
URLs carry state. React Router gives hooks to read and change it.

### Dynamic segments - `useParams`

```jsx
<Route path="/users/:userId" element={<User />} />

function User() {
  const { userId } = useParams();   // always a string!
}
```

Convert numbers yourself: `Number(userId)`. Optional segments use `:id?` and splats use `*`.

### Query string - `useSearchParams`

```jsx
const [params, setParams] = useSearchParams();
const q = params.get("q") ?? "";
setParams({ q: "react", page: "2" });
```

It works like `useState`, but the state lives in the URL, so it survives refresh and can be shared. Ideal for filters, search, sorting and pagination.

### Programmatic navigation - `useNavigate`

```jsx
const navigate = useNavigate();
navigate("/orders/42");
navigate(-1);                       // back
navigate("/login", { replace: true, state: { from: location } });
```

Use it after forms or login. Use `<Navigate to="/login" replace />` when you want to redirect during render.

### Location and state

`useLocation()` returns `pathname`, `search`, `hash` and `state` (data passed through `navigate`, not visible in URL).

### Tips

- Prefer `Link` for normal navigation; use `navigate` for side-effect-driven moves.
- `replace` avoids filling the back-button history with redirects.

topics.title: Data Routers: Loaders and Actions
topics.summary: Fetch data before rendering a route and handle form submissions with loader and action functions.
topics.description:
The **data router** API (`createBrowserRouter` + `RouterProvider`) lets a route declare its data needs next to its path. This avoids "render, then fetch in an effect, then show spinner" waterfalls.

```jsx
const router = createBrowserRouter([
  {
    path: "/",
    element: <Root />,
    errorElement: <ErrorPage />,
    children: [
      {
        path: "posts/:id",
        loader: ({ params }) => fetch(`/api/posts/${params.id}`).then(r => r.json()),
        action: async ({ request }) => { /* handle form POST */ },
        element: <Post />,
      },
    ],
  },
]);
<RouterProvider router={router} />
```

### Pieces

- **`loader`** - runs before the route renders (in parallel for nested routes). Read in the component with `useLoaderData()`.
- **`action`** - handles `<Form method="post">` submissions and `fetcher.submit`. After an action, loaders **revalidate** automatically so the UI stays in sync.
- **`errorElement`** - renders if the loader, action or component throws. Read the error with `useRouteError()`.
- **`useNavigation()`** - `state` is `idle | loading | submitting` for global progress bars.
- **`useFetcher()`** - call loaders/actions without navigating (like buttons, inline edits).
- **`defer` / `Await`** (v6) or streaming promises (v7) - render fast parts first.

### Why use it

Parallel data loading, built-in error handling, no spinners-in-spinners, and automatic revalidation after mutations. In React Router v7 framework mode it adds SSR, type-safe loaders and file-based or config routes.

### With TanStack Query

You can call `queryClient.ensureQueryData` inside a loader to combine caching with route-level fetching.

topics.title: Protected Routes and Auth Redirects
topics.summary: Guard routes by checking authentication and redirect unauthenticated users to login, remembering where they wanted to go.
topics.description:
Some pages (dashboard, profile, checkout) require a logged-in user. A **protected route** is a wrapper that checks auth and either renders the page or redirects.

### Pattern: guard layout route

```jsx
function RequireAuth() {
  const { user, loading } = useAuth();
  const location = useLocation();

  if (loading) return <Spinner />;               // still checking session
  if (!user) return <Navigate to="/login" replace state={{ from: location }} />;
  return <Outlet />;                              // render child routes
}

<Route element={<RequireAuth />}>
  <Route path="/dashboard" element={<Dashboard />} />
  <Route path="/profile" element={<Profile />} />
</Route>
```

### After login

Read `location.state?.from` and `navigate(from, { replace: true })` so users land where they were headed.

### Details that matter

- **Loading state:** on refresh the auth status is unknown for a moment. Show a spinner; otherwise logged-in users are bounced to login.
- **Role-based access:** `RequireRole role="admin"` renders 403 or redirects.
- **Public-only routes:** redirect logged-in users away from `/login`.
- **Store auth in a context** (`AuthProvider` with `useAuth`), initialize from a cookie/session check.

### Security reminder

Route guards are only **UX**. Anyone can read your JavaScript bundle. Real protection is on the **server**: every API call must verify the token/session and permissions. Prefer HttpOnly cookies for session tokens over localStorage.

Redirect with <Navigate replace state={{ from }}>

pitfalls: Redirecting to login while auth state is still loading.
Hiding admin pages only on the client and trusting it for security.

topics.title: Lazy Routes, 404s and Scroll Handling
topics.summary: Code-split pages with React.lazy or the router's lazy property, and handle not-found and scroll behavior.
topics.description:
Each page of a big app should load only when visited. Combine routing with code splitting.

### With React.lazy and Suspense

```jsx
const Dashboard = lazy(() => import("./pages/Dashboard"));

<Suspense fallback={<PageSpinner />}>
  <Routes>
    <Route path="/dashboard" element={<Dashboard />} />
  </Routes>
</Suspense>
```

### With the data router `lazy` property

```jsx
{ path: "dashboard", lazy: () => import("./pages/Dashboard") }
```

The module exports `Component`, `loader`, `action` and `ErrorBoundary`, and the router loads it only when needed. This also loads the code in parallel with the data.

### 404 and error pages

- `path="*"` for unknown URLs.
- In the data router use `errorElement` for thrown errors; throw `new Response("Not found", { status: 404 })` from loaders for missing resources.
- Show a friendly page with a link home. Remember the server should also return a 404 status for SSR apps.

### Scroll and focus

- SPA navigation does not reset scroll. Use `<ScrollRestoration />` (data routers) or a small effect that scrolls to top on `pathname` change.
- Move focus to the main heading after navigation for screen reader users and update `document.title`.

### Prefetching

Call the import function on link hover (`onMouseEnter={() => import("./pages/Dashboard")}`) for instant navigation. React Router v7 `<Link prefetch="intent">` does this in framework mode.
